label: Steering the sampler with physics potentials
context: A 2D ligand (6 atoms, small hexagon-ish) being placed into a protein pocket (protein drawn as a curved wall of 14 grey atoms with radii). Phase 1 'plain sampling': over sampling steps the ligand converges, but ends slightly overlapping the wall: draw the clashing atom pairs with red overlap highlights and a label 'steric clash'. Phase 2 'steered sampling': same run, but at each step show a small warm arrow on each clashing atom = −∇ of a clash potential, pushing atoms apart; also a 'chirality / bond length' check icon; the ligand ends without clashes. Show a step counter and a small energy bar 'potential E(x)' that drops under steering. Caption: 'Boltz-1x / Boltz-2: between denoising steps, nudge x down the gradient of physical penalty terms; the network is unchanged'. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.
